name: Idiopathic Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection

criteria.description: Angiographic demonstration of non-atherosclerotic coronary artery dissection with characteristic appearance
Lack of significant atherosclerotic coronary artery disease on imaging
Presentation with acute coronary syndrome symptoms without precipitating trauma or iatrogenic cause
Exclusion of other causes of coronary dissection such as connective tissue disorders or vasculitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Angiographic evidence of coronary artery dissection plus absence of atherosclerosis and clinical presentation consistent with acute coronary syndrome
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Coronary angiography or intracoronary imaging (OCT/IVUS) is essential for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically severe and acute in nature

pathognomonic.symptomName: Electrocardiographic changes consistent with acute myocardial ischemia

common.symptomName: Dyspnea on exertion or at rest
searchTerms: shortness of breath with activity or rest
difficulty breathing on exertion or at rest

occasional.notes: May occur due to arrhythmia or ischemia

searchTerms: back pain spreading from chest area
pain radiating from chest to back
feelings of anxiety or panic attacks
episodes of intense fear or anxiety
stroke caused by heart artery clot
cerebral infarction due to heart embolus

laboratory: Elevated cardiac troponin I or T
imaging: Coronary angiography showing characteristic dissection flap or intramural hematoma
Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) or optical coherence tomography (OCT) confirming arterial wall dissection
Echocardiogram showing regional wall motion abnormalities
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; some association with connective tissue disorder genes in secondary cases
other: Absence of atherosclerotic plaques in affected vessels
Possible fibromuscular dysplasia in extracoronary arteries

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of atherosclerotic plaques on angiography
Risk factors such as hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking
Vessel wall thickening and inflammation on imaging

redFlags: Sudden onset severe chest pain with ECG changes
Sudden cardiac arrest or ventricular arrhythmias
references: Saw J. Spontaneous coronary artery dissection. Can J Cardiol. 2013;29(9):1027-1033.
Tweet MS, Hayes SN, Pitta SR, et al. Clinical features, management, and prognosis of spontaneous coronary artery dissection. Circulation. 2012;126(5):579-588.
